chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Hakam al-Hannat, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Connecting with the relatives and good neighborliness build up the dwellings and increase the lifespans.'

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ: Good neighborliness / good conduct towards neighbors

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of maintaining family ties and good neighborly relations in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links social cohesion to divine blessing, asserting that kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and neighborly kindness (husn al-jiwar) are instrumental in both the material prosperity of dwellings and the extension of human lifespan. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the interplay between ethical conduct and metaphysical outcomes, where maintaining family and community bonds serves as a means of attracting barakah. The narration underscores the holistic view of well-being in Islamic tradition, where social stability directly influences individual longevity and domestic flourishing.
